command: verify({ check: 'assembly-path', file: 'examples/assemblies/assembly-stability-bracket.kcad.ts', sequence: true, stability: true })

tessellation.source: meshShapeForExport default: relative linear 0.01, angular 0.05 rad; per-face fallback absolute 0.02 mm, 0.1 rad

model.clearancePolicy: Zero clearance: any positive-travel triangle contact blocks; t=0 departure is free.

limitations: Local watertight mesh validation, not BREP or hardware acceptance. Positive-travel contact is conservatively blocked; starting contact may also block sliding. Mesh tessellation approximates curves. Straight translation and declared helical fastener motion only; no mate solving, deformation, thread engagement or torque. Press/snap fits are declared, never simulated. Tool reach is a swept-envelope approximation, not a driver drawing. Static stability is approximate: a centre-of-mass projection onto a support polygon of mesh contacts with already-stable parts, not gravity simulation, friction, tipping or fixture analysis. A needs-hold finding names an external hold the model cannot prove. Subassembly and multi-part moves are heuristic, not exhaustive. Sampling paths are found-by-search, never proven. Blocked and unknown parts are not "impossible".
